title: Runner v0.112.0 released but not deployed: a rejected-lease race failed main CI
summary: The merge of echopoint-runner#126 (transport retries) released tag `v0.112.0` at 17:07Z, but the main CI test job failed on `TestRejectedLeaseStopsTheRunBeforeItsNextRequest`, so no container image was built and no deploy was dispatched. The dev and prod self-hosted runner services kept running v0.111.0 (`main-d159a21`), while echopoint-cli v5.0.1 already embeds v0.112.0. The test failed because `markJobRejected` cancelled the run before it recorded the rejection, so the cancelled run checked `isRejected`, saw false and sent a failure completion. The race existed since the first runner snapshot and failed CI once in about 40 main runs. The fix records the rejection first; it ships with this postmortem and deploys the retries.

impact.text: No customer impact. Self-hosted runs on dev and prod (monitors, the public status probe, the self-hosted CI monitor) kept running without the transport retries of v0.112.0 for about 1.5 h, while Ephemeral runs through CLI v5.0.1 had them. In production the race had no effect: every one of the 35 heartbeat rejections since 2026-10-20 came after the job had finished.

runner services on v0.112.0 after the release

trigger: Main CI run [44573501171](https://github.com/nanostack-dev/echopoint-runner/actions/runs/44573501171) for caf812c failed `TestRejectedLeaseStopsTheRunBeforeItsNextRequest`; the image build and the dev deploy dispatch were skipped.
detection: The `echopoint-investigation` routine saw at 18:1xZ that the runner services still logged `app.commit` `main-d159a21` an hour after the `v0.112.0` release. A failed main CI on the runner notifies nobody, and the PR body said the merge deploys the runners.
resolution: The fix records the rejection in the rejected map before it cancels the run, so a cancelled run always sees the rejection and sends no completion. Its merge releases the next tag, builds the image and deploys both fixes.

whys.problem: Runner v0.112.0 was released and pinned by CLI v5.0.1, but the dev and prod runner services never got it

because.text: The main CI test job failed, so `Build and Push Container Image` and `Dispatch Deploy (dev)` were skipped
because.evidence: [Run 44573501171](https://github.com/nanostack-dev/echopoint-runner/actions/runs/44573501171): Test failure, the two later jobs skipped

because.text: `TestRejectedLeaseStopsTheRunBeforeItsNextRequest` got a nil error: the rejected run sent a failure completion
because.evidence: Log: `runner job failed` with `context canceled`, no `skipping failure completion for rejected runner job` line

because.text: `markJobRejected` cancels the run before it writes the rejected map, and the woken run checks `isRejected` in that gap
because.evidence: `internal/runtime/runtime.go` markJobRejected; a 50 ms sleep after the cancel fails the test 5 of 5 times, and passes with the fix

because.text: The test leaves the gap to the scheduler: it passed 400 local runs and the PR check, and failed once in about 40 main runs
because.evidence: Main `Go Build and Test` history since 2026-10-07: first failure on caf812c

because.text: A rejection is two pieces of state written in the wrong order: the signal (cancel) before the fact (rejected map) it reports
The release tag exists although the code failed its tests, so a consumer pinned an undeployed version
because.evidence: `release.yml` runs on every push to main; v0.112.0 tagged at 17:07:08Z, tests failed at 17:08:15Z

because.text: Release and Go Build and Test are separate workflows on the same push, and Release does not wait for the tests
Release tagging is not gated on a green main test run
Nobody saw the skipped deploy for an hour, and the CLI release went ahead
because.evidence: CLI v5.0.1 at 17:22Z; PR body of #126 says the merge deploys the runners

because.text: A failed main CI on echopoint-runner sends no alert, and no check compares the runner services' version with the latest release
Nothing checks that a released runner version reaches the runner services

contributing: Every push to main releases a version, so the tag is cut minutes before the tests finish.

well: A 50 ms sleep at the suspected gap reproduced the failure at once, which proved the cause before the fix.
Lease rejections in production all came after completion, so the race never sent a wrong completion there.
wrong: The merge author released the CLI on the assumption that the merge had deployed the runners.
A red main run on a merged commit was the only signal.
lucky: The skipped deploy only delayed a retry improvement; a skipped security fix would have stayed undeployed the same way.
No production lease was rejected mid-run in 30 days, where the race would have sent a completion for a reassigned job.

actions.what: Record the rejection before cancelling the run in `markJobRejected`
Tag a release only after `Go Build and Test` passed on that main commit (or tag from the go.yml run)
The flow routine compares the runner services' `app.commit` with runner main HEAD every run
Alert when the echopoint-runner main CI fails after a merge
Deployment runbook: after a merge, confirm the main run is green and the services log `main-<sha>`

messaging.internal: Runner v0.112.0 (transport retries) was tagged but never deployed: main CI failed on a rejected-lease race. Fix records the rejection before cancelling; its merge deploys both.
